info.description:
REST API for creating, driving, and destroying isolated sandboxes for AI agents.
Sandboxes are built directly on Linux namespaces, cgroups v2, overlayfs, seccomp, and capabilities. They share the host kernel, so they are weaker than hardware-backed microVMs.
The source of truth remains the codebase; this spec is generated from handler annotations.
info.title: sandboxd API

get.description: Lists the base root filesystems sandboxes can be created from. Images are imported by the operator with `sandboxdctl image import`.
Lists sandboxes held by this server, including recently stopped or failed ones that are still within the tombstone retention window.

post.description: Creates an isolated environment (user, mount, pid, net, uts, ipc and cgroup namespaces; cgroup v2 limits; overlay root on a size-capped tmpfs; seccomp) and waits until it is running. Omitted limits use the server defaults; values above the server maximums are rejected.

400.description: Validation failed, or a limit exceeds the server maximum (limit_exceeded).

get.description: Returns the sandbox state, limits, and timestamps. Running sandboxes also include live resource statistics.

delete.description: Kills every process in the sandbox and releases its cgroup, mounts, storage, and network. Idempotent for sandboxes that are already stopped.

500.description: Teardown failed; the sandbox is marked failed.

post.description: Runs one command in the sandbox as the unprivileged sandbox user and waits for it to finish. `command` runs through /bin/sh -c; `argv` runs directly. On timeout the command's whole process group is killed and timed_out is true. stdout and stderr are each capped at SANDBOX_EXEC_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES; excess output is dropped and flagged as truncated.

400.description: Validation failed, or timeout above the server maximum.

429.description: Too many concurrent commands in this sandbox (exec_limit_reached).

post.description: Same request as POST /exec, but responds with Server-Sent Events as output arrives: `stdout` and `stderr` events carry {"data": "..."}; the final `exit` event carries {"result": {...}} (stdout/stderr omitted), or an `error` event carries {"error": "..."}. Validation and lookup failures before the command starts are returned as regular JSON errors. Disconnecting kills the command.
post.summary: Run a command and stream its output

200.description: Event stream; each data line is one ExecStreamEvent.

get.description: Streams a regular file from the sandbox. The path is resolved inside the sandbox root, so symlinks and `..` can never reach the host filesystem.

parameters.description: Absolute file path inside the sandbox.
parameters.name: path

409.description: Sandbox not running, or the path is a directory.

put.description: Writes the raw request body to a file inside the sandbox, creating or truncating it. Parent directories must exist. New files are owned by the sandbox user. The body is streamed and capped at SANDBOX_FILE_MAX_BYTES, and also counts against the sandbox's storage_mb.

parameters.description: Absolute file path inside the sandbox.
parameters.name: path

parameters.description: Octal permission for a new file.
parameters.name: mode

404.description: Sandbox or parent directory not found.

409.description: Sandbox not running, or the path is a directory.

delete.description: Removes a file, symlink, or empty directory; recursive=true removes non-empty directories. The sandbox root cannot be removed.

409.description: Sandbox not running, or the directory is not empty.

get.description: Lists the entries of a directory inside the sandbox, sorted by name. Symlinks are reported, not followed.

parameters.description: Absolute directory path inside the sandbox.
parameters.name: path

409.description: Sandbox not running, or the path is not a directory.

post.description: Creates a directory owned by the sandbox user; with parents=true missing parents are created too and an existing directory is not an error.

409.description: Sandbox not running, or the path already exists.

get.description: Returns metadata for a path inside the sandbox without following a final symlink.

post.description: Resets the expiry to now + ttl_seconds (default SANDBOX_DEFAULT_TTL), never beyond SANDBOX_MAX_TTL after creation, and counts as activity for the idle timeout.
Starts a long-lived shell inside the sandbox. Commands sent to the session share shell state -- working directory, exported variables, activated virtualenvs -- across calls.

400.description: Validation failed, or the session limit is reached.

delete.description: Kills the session shell and everything it started.

post.description: Writes the command to the session shell and waits for it to finish. A session runs one command at a time. If the command times out the session is terminated, because its shell state is no longer known.
post.summary: Run a command in a shell session

409.description: Sandbox not running, session busy (session_busy), or session closed (session_closed).

get.description: Returns cgroup memory, CPU, process, and OOM counters plus writable-layer usage.

Upgrades to a WebSocket attached to a login shell on a pseudo-terminal inside the sandbox: a new one, or with terminal_id a running one (recent output is replayed). Binary messages carry raw terminal input (client to server) and output (server to client). Text messages carry JSON control messages: the server first sends {"type":"attached","terminal_id":"..."}; the client sends {"type":"resize","cols":N,"rows":N} and {"type":"close"} to end the terminal; the server sends {"type":"exit","exit_code":N} or {"type":"error","error":"..."} before closing. Closing the socket without "close" detaches: the shell keeps running for SANDBOX_TERMINAL_DETACH_TIMEOUT and can be reattached; a newer attachment takes over from an older one. Authenticate with a bearer key or with a ticket from POST /terminal/tickets; browser Origins must be this server or an allowed CORS origin. While attached, the terminal keeps the sandbox from going idle.

parameters.description: Login shell; bash falls back to sh when absent.
parameters.name: shell

401.description: Missing or invalid API key or ticket.

post.description: Returns a single-use ticket, valid for 30 seconds, that authenticates one WebSocket upgrade on GET /api/v1/sandboxes/{id}/terminal. Browsers need it because they cannot send an Authorization header on a WebSocket.

get.description: Returns 204 when the process is alive.

Reports whether the sandbox engine passed its preflight checks (Linux, cgroup v2 delegation, overlayfs, openat2) and can create sandboxes.
The response includes build info. In environments whose APP_ENV contains "prod" or "staging", checks is returned as an empty object so internal errors are not exposed; the status code (200 or 503) still reflects engine health.

build_time.description: BuildTime is the UTC image build time.

commit.description: Commit is the seven-character Git commit hash.

modified.description: Modified reports whether Go detected local source changes.

tag.description: Tag is the release tag, or unknown when the build is not tagged.

version.description: Version is formatted for the deployment environment.

cpu_millis.description: CPUMillis is the CPU quota in millicores (1000 = one full core).

env.description: Env is applied to every command run in the sandbox.

idle_timeout_seconds.description: IdleTimeoutSeconds destroys the sandbox after this long without exec or file activity; 0 uses the server default.

image.description: Image is the base root filesystem; defaults to SANDBOX_DEFAULT_IMAGE.

labels.description: Labels are opaque caller metadata usable as list filters.

memory_mb.description: MemoryMB is the hard memory limit; exceeding it OOM-kills the sandbox's processes.

network.description: Network is none (loopback only) or egress (outbound internet, private ranges blocked).

pids_max.description: PidsMax caps the number of processes and threads.

storage_mb.description: StorageMB caps the writable layer; writes beyond it fail with ENOSPC.

ttl_seconds.description: TTLSeconds is the lifetime after which the sandbox is destroyed.

cwd.description: Cwd is the initial working directory.

env.description: Env is exported into the session shell at startup.

shell.description: Shell is the interpreter kept alive for the session; bash falls back to sh when absent.

user.description:
User runs the session's shell as root or the sandbox user; defaults to
SANDBOX_DEFAULT_USER.
